output.brief:
The Android login drop is not caused by release 6.14, the password screen, the OS patch, or bots. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC the edge vendor (Corvane) activated a new rule, AUTO-LIB-17. It blocks any password-login request from the app's networking library, nettle-http, that has no edge session cookie. Those requests get a 403. The blocked requests come from about 41,300 install IDs, and 92% of those had logged in successfully in the prior 90 days, so they look like real customers. The failures started within a minute of the rule going live, on every app version and OS version. 6.14 is only 5% of attempts and fails at the same rate as older versions. Quick-unlock and iOS are unaffected. Password success fell from 96.0% to 8.2%.

Next step: ask Corvane to set the new rule to log-only on the mobile password path. Keep rate limits, lockout and other rules on. Then check in telemetry that password success returns to about 96%. Don't roll back 6.14. Don't raise bot sensitivity. Don't exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. Either would hide or worsen the problem. Confidence is high. The remaining uncertainty is the contact-centre call rise, which also has other causes.
